To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

diffuse IPS is more effective than patterned IPS in eliciting a photoparoxysrnal response in patients with persistent seizures and that the response is more frequent in patients who had a seizure within 3 days of testing.

the presence of a photic driving response to IPS in patients with epilepsy is associated with a higher risk for seizure recurrence and that the risk is higher when the response is to diffuse stimulation.
diffuse IPS (flicker) is more sensitive in detecting photosensitive epilepsy and that the absence of PCR to diffuse IPS is a better predictor for seizure control.

the assessment of seizure control in photosensitive epilepsy patients.
the assessment of photosensitivity in patients with epilepsy, using IPS.
the study of visual evoked responses in patients with epilepsy, using different stimuli.

diffuse IPS is a better predictor of the seizure outcome than patterned IPS.

photosensitive epilepsy patients who are seizure-free show a differential response to IPS, when compared to patients who are not seizure-free.
